name: Grand Prix de l'automobile Club de France

nar.text: The day of the race, a Monday, was a clear sunny morning
exactly at eight o'clock René de Knyff, President of the ACF Sporting Commission, lowered the yellow flag for the rolling start.
Bordino's red Fiat from the second row in a spurt passed Guinness (Sunbeam) and Thomas (Delage) and held the lead when passing the last grandstands.
Vizcaya crashes into the fencing at La Membrolle in the dust; the Bugatti is out.
After the first lap Bordino (Fiat) had eclipsed all his practice times, leading after 9m45s. He was 41 seconds clear of Guinness (Sunbeam), Thomas (Delage) and Giaccone (Fiat).
On the third lap Thomas dropped from third to eighth place as his engine overheated.
Segrave fell behind with his clutch slipping. Divo gained fourth place when he passed Salamano's Fiat who had scraped along the barrier at Semblançay and lost over two minutes.
Marco retires his Bugatti on the downhill before the finish.
Bordino leads Guinness by 2m20s after five laps.
Thomas retires the overheating Delage from fifth place.
He started again but retired on lap eight with a broken oil pump.
After the eighth lap Bordino led Guinness by 3m49s
Bordino stops after Membrolle, rejoins, stops again and retires.
After Bordino's retirement, Guinness in the Sunbeam found himself leading the French Grand Prix, which was the first time in Grand Prix history that a green car from Britain led the field.
Prince de Cystria drove into the soft sand at La Membrolle hairpin.
At the end of the eleventh lap, Divo stopped at his pit to drop off his mechanic Hivernet, who had been injured by a flying stone and took Moriceau on board.
Guinness stopped on the 13th lap for fuel, oil and water. As the Sunbeam left his pit, Guinness lost his lead as both Fiats passed
On lap 14, Guinness dropped from third to sixth place, losing around 10 minutes at the pits due to a slipping clutch which advanced Divo into third place.
On the 17th lap Giaccone stopped at the pits, changed spark plugs, rear wheel and refilled fuel and oil.
Salamano takes the lead.
On lap 18, Guyot in second place stopped for around seven minutes and rejoined in fourth place while Divo gained second place.
On lap 19, Salamano stopped for about 5 minutes at his pits, refilled fuel and oil and changed one wheel. He rejoined in second place, while Divo had taken the lead.
Giaccone stops again, works ten minutes on the car and retires; broken exhaust valve.
When Rougier retired the Voisin, the field was down to eight cars.
On lap 22 Salamano passed Divo, maintaining a race speed of nearly 125 km/h.
Guyot retires with a broken oil pump.
On the 31st lap Salamano was in the lead when Divo in second place stopped to refuel. But the fuel tank filler cap was unknowingly turned the wrong way by mistake, and seized.
More than 15 minutes were spent trying to loosen the cap with a variety of tools.
On lap 33, the leading Fiat of Salamano failed to appear past the grandstands at the expected time. The car had stopped apparently out of fuel.
Then Segrave arrived at the stands in first place after 6h12m35s.
Totally exhausted, Ferretti reached his pits after a two kilometer sprint.
Divo stopped now every lap to refill his spare fuel can, losing much time.
On the last lap Guinness lost about two minutes at La Membrolle, when he stalled the car with a problem of restarting the engine due to his valves being badly burnt.
Segrave wins in 6h35m19.6s; Divo is a lap down.
